note: Tokiwasan Maru (1,804 t) and Shoryu Maru (1,916 t) of convoy No. 3905, Yokosuka to Haha-jima, both sunk. BANG claimed a medium AK and a medium AO (Attacks 1-2, 1616-1632 K). Secondary source only
No. 2 Tosei Maru (507-ton tanker) of convoy TAKA-909 sunk. BANG claimed one AK sunk and another probably sunk (Attacks 3-4); the escorts claimed BANG sunk

The Japanese record of the same sinkings (J01 is the secondary account): Shoryu and Tokiwasan Maru sunk at 1520 I, 4 minutes after BANG's first salvo. Its position, a bearing from Sumisu-jima, is about 188 nm from BANG's; the names and the time pair them, the place does not
Second salvo 16 minutes after the first; the Japanese record has both ships sunk at 1520 I
